summary.intent: The user asked whether any subagents were still running, wanting a status check on background work in the session.
summary.outcome: The assistant reported six subagents still running (slice-s7a2, condition-map-memo, prefetch-spike, slice-s8a, clean-scripts, clean-code), that finished ones need no further action, and that peer sessions belong to others and were left alone. It proposed waiting or stopping the idle callisto-cleanup teammate, and gave a merge order.

repo: Work is split across parallel subagents, each owning a distinct branch and PR.
Planned merge order: PR #429 first because it unblocks main, then #428, then the rest as their PRs open.
Trail items #355 (keep only scripts that add value) and #356 (delete unused code) are being handled by the clean-scripts and clean-code subagents.
workflow: Peer sessions (caliper-article, monokl-v1, plugin-audit, road-to-alpha-callisto, cleanup-merged-branches-worktrees, and offline Remote Control ones) belong to other sessions and should not be stopped by this session.
Idle teammates such as callisto-cleanup hold no work and can be stopped to shorten the agent list.
Subagents that keep resending a finished report waste tokens; stop them, as was done with the #426 finding worker.

friction: A subagent re-reporting that it is waiting on its own background work previously wasted tokens, and could recur.
The long list of running, completed, idle, and peer sessions makes it hard to tell which agents are actually active.
open_items: Wait for the six running subagents to finish: slice-s7a2, condition-map-memo, prefetch-spike, slice-s8a, clean-scripts, clean-code.
Optionally stop the idle callisto-cleanup teammate.
Merge PRs in order as they land: #429, then #428, then the rest.
Watch for subagents resending finished reports and stop them if so.
